79,000/- per hectare for the Dry Crop Land and Rs. 1,500/- per hectare for the Potkharab land
. The Appellant(s) filed the Reference under Section 18 of the L.A. Act for enhancement in the compensation and then led the evidence.

The learned Reference Court determined the rate of Rs.
1,44,000/- per hectare for the Dry Crop Land and Rs. 72,000/- per hectare for Potkharab land.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Appellant(s) that, the learned Reference Court ignored the evidence on record, which shows that, there was a well and orange trees on the acquired land.

There was ample material on record to show that, the acquired land was the perennially irrigated land and the learned Reference Court considered the same as the 'Dry Crop Land', which was contrary to the evidence on record.
It is submitted that, the acquired land being perennially irrigated land, the double rate should be determined.
He further submitted that, for the well, the valuation made by the Valuer needs to be considered.
He submitted that, the rate of Rs. 3,000/- per tree for the big orange trees and Rs. 1,000/- per tree for the small orange trees needs to be considered on the basis of guesswork.
He submitted that, by allowing the Appeal, the impugned judgment and award be suitably modified.

4. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Acquiring Body that, the observations made by the learned Reference Court shows that, there was no evidence to show the existence of well, the existence of orange trees and the existence of irrigation facility in the acquired land.

It is submitted that, the 5 15) FA 1190-2013-J.odt learned Reference Court has rightly appreciated the evidence on record and considered the acquired land as the Dry Crop Land, and in absence of any evidence, did not determine the compensation for the trees and the well.
He submits that, the Appeal be dismissed.

5. It is submitted by the learned AGP for the State that, in absence of any evidence to prove that, the acquired land was irrigated land, no interference is called for in the impugned judgment and award.
6.
With the assistance of both the sides, perused the papers.

It is observed by the learned Reference Court in para 9 of the judgment that, as can be seen from the copy of Horticulture Report at Exh. 32,
the existence of actual orange trees were not found by the concerned Agricultural/Horticulture Officer, as mentioned in Column no. 5-A of Exh. 32.

It is further observed in para 14 of the impugned judgment that, the abstracts issued by the witness no. 2 examined by the Claimant, did not bear the date, month and year of his visit on the spot and there was admission by this witness no. 2 that, the water level of wells are not mentioned in his report.

The learned Reference Court 6 15) FA 1190-2013-J.odt observed that, the water level was the most significant aspect in order to determine the potentiality and capacity of the wells while considering the amount of enhanced compensation, and awarded the compensation of Rs. 40,000/- for the well.

Considering the judgment at Exh. 36/Exh. 40, in which the rate of Rs. 1,25,000/- per hectare was determined, the learned Reference Court considering the 10% increase in the market value, determined the rate for Rs. 1,44,000/- per hectare considering the acquired land as the 'Dry Crop Land'.

sentences.text: Though Exh.32, which is the Appendix-E (Statement of Valuation of Fruit Trees) issued by the office of LAO does not show the number of trees in Column 5A (i.e. Actual), the Column no. 5 shows that, as per Joint Measurement Report (JMR), there were 55 big trees and 204 small trees and their future age is mentioned in Column 9A of the said Appendix-E as 8 and 17 years, respectively.

A copy of award speaks that, the concerned Government Machinery conducted the panchnama in respect of orange trees and the well in the acquired land and submitted the report in the office of LAO and the valuation of the fruit bearing trees was done by the Agricultural Officer.

It speaks that, on the 7 15)
FA 1190-2013-J.odt basis of communication from the TILR, since the trees and the well were not found in existence, the award was declared without determining the compensation for the same.
8. The Abstract Sheet at Exh.43 in respect of construction of 'Open Dug Well' shows the expenditure incurred.
The said Abstract Sheet showing the costs of the well, is brought on record in the evidence of witness no.2.

A copy of panchanama below Exh.33 prepared by the Government Machinery and forwarded vide communication dated 21/07/2004 from the office of Sub-Divisional Engineer,
Laghu Patbandhare Up-vibhag, Morshi, District Amravati to the SLAO (Special Land Acquisition Officer), shows the acquired land as the Bagayat land and there is clear reference of constructed well and 55 big orange trees and 204 small orange trees.
The said panchanama is undisputedly prepared by the Government Machinery.

There is 'Gao Namuna Seven' extract of the acquired land at Exh. 41,
which shows the existence of orange trees.
9.

The above referred documents on the record clearly indicate that, the acquired land was having the well and fruit bearing trees, which go to show that, the acquired land was 8 15) FA 1190-2013-J.odt irrigated land.

The aforesaid observations in the award that, it was informed from the office of TILR that, at the time of joint measurement, no orange trees and well were found on the acquired land, is contrary to the Exh. 32-Appendix-E (Statement of Valuation of Fruit Trees).

Therefore, in the backdrop of the said material on record, the contention of the learned counsel for the Appellant that, the acquired land was perennially irrigated land and therefore, the double rate will have to be granted has merit.
As regards the clear evidence of the existence of the orange trees and no evidence in respect of the rate per orange tree, some guesswork is required to be done.
As per Exh. 32, the future life of 55 orange trees is shown eight (8) years, for which, Rs. 3,000/- per orange tree would be appropriate compensation.

The future age of 204 orange trees is shown seventeen (17)
years, for which, Rs. 1,000/- per orange tree would be appropriate compensation.
The compensation for well is maintained without any enhancement.
With this discussion, the impugned judgment and award needs modification.
Hence, the following order:-
ORDER I) The Appeal is partly allowed.
The Appellant(s) would be entitled for the rate of Rs. 2,88,000/- per hectare for the irrigated acquired land.
III) The Appellant(s) shall be entitled for the compensation of Rs. 3,000/- per orange tree for 55 orange trees and Rs. 1,000/- per orange tree for 204 orange trees.
IV) The compensation for the well is maintained.
V) The statutory benefits be calculated on the enhanced amount of compensation.
